name: Target
summary: Build the foundation for Brigade life through BB knowledge, citizenship, faith or character education, and recruit drill.
learn: The Brigade’s Object, Motto, history, ranks, uniform, songs, and award scheme
National symbols, the anthem, and knowledge of the local neighbourhood
Introductory faith or character lessons and basic recruit drill
classActivities: Create a squad quiz covering the BB Object, Motto, history, ranks, and uniform care.
Identify the national flag and coat of arms, then make a neighbourhood information sheet.
Practise recruit drill and discuss the introductory faith or character lessons with an Officer.

name: Christian Education
summary: Explore Scripture and put Christian faith into practice through personal relationships, ministry, and community life.
learn: Understanding a Bible passage and applying it in everyday life
Prayer, devotion, worship, and healthy personal relationships
Sharing faith, serving in ministry, and understanding community relationships
classActivities: Read a chosen Bible passage and discuss how it applies to a friendship or family situation.
Develop a personal prayer and devotion plan, then reflect on what is learned.
Plan a supervised ministry contribution and discuss how it serves the church or Sponsoring Body.

name: Drill
summary: Develop discipline, self-control, and confidence through personal drill, squad teamwork, commanding, and instruction.
learn: Static drill, marching, squad movements, and correct uniform presentation
Drill theory, words of command, and paying compliments
Advanced Colour Party and Guard of Honour drill and teaching recruits
classActivities: Practise static movements and marching in a squad using the current BBM Drill Manual.
Take turns giving commands and explaining the purpose of each command.
Prepare an instructor-supervised lesson that teaches a recruit a basic drill movement.

name: Recruitment
summary: Learn to welcome new members and support company growth through recruiting, programme planning, and communication.
learn: Introducing Brigade life to prospective members
Planning recruiting talks, displays, and committee work
Helping new recruits settle in through a sustained programme
classActivities: Prepare and rehearse a short recruiting talk for a church, school, or community audience.
Design an Officer-approved exhibition or presentation explaining the company’s activities.
Draft a three-month welcome programme that includes introductory Target Award learning.

name: Arts
summary: Develop creative expression through an approved individual or group arts project with regular assessment and a final presentation.
learn: Creative skills in an approved area such as drawing, drama, music, or writing
Planning a project and recording progress where required
Presenting finished work for assessment
classActivities: Plan an Officer-approved drawing or painting project and present work at agreed progress reviews.
Develop a group drama or mime piece under an instructor’s guidance.
Prepare a short written or visual presentation explaining the completed creative work.

name: Craft
summary: Build practical making skills through an approved craft project, with different activities at Basic and Advanced levels.
learn: Hands-on techniques in an approved craft such as origami, sewing, or model making
Planning, making, and documenting a practical project
Reviewing progress and presenting completed work
classActivities: Propose an origami or model-making project for Officer approval and plan its materials.
Practise a selected craft technique in an instructor-led class, then develop a finished piece.
Keep a project record and explain the making process when presenting the final work.

name: Hobbies
summary: Explore a personal interest through an approved hobby project that develops skills, records progress, and produces assessable work.
learn: Skills in an approved interest such as astronomy, photography, or cycle maintenance
Developing a hobby through regular practice and review
Recording work and presenting the results of a project
classActivities: Plan an Officer-approved photography project and review the results at regular intervals.
Learn basic cycle maintenance with an instructor and record the work completed.
Prepare a short presentation or display that shares the outcome of a chosen hobby project.

name: Athletics
summary: Improve fitness and athletic performance through track and field events measured against the handbook’s award standards.
learn: Running and hurdling techniques for track events
Jumping and throwing techniques for field events
Measuring performance and preparing for the required event standards
classActivities: Rotate through instructor-led running, jumping, and throwing practice stations.
Record practice times and distances and compare them with the applicable handbook standards.
Prepare a training plan covering two track events and two field events.

name: Bandsman
summary: Develop brass or woodwind musicianship through music theory, instrument care, sight-reading, scales, and band performance.
learn: Music theory and sight-reading at the appropriate level
Care of a brass or woodwind instrument and confident ensemble playing
Scales, arpeggios, and pieces in contrasting tempos
classActivities: Practise an instructor-selected scale and explain the correct care of the instrument.
Sight-read a short passage and work on timing with other band members.
Rehearse contrasting fast and slow pieces for a supervised band performance.

name: Buglers
summary: Develop bugle playing through recognised calls, music theory, instrument care, and active participation in a BB band.
learn: Recognising and playing the prescribed basic bugle calls
Music theory, sight-reading, and instrument maintenance
Additional calls and continued public band performance at Advanced level
classActivities: Listen to and identify calls such as Reveille, Fall-In, and Last Post before practising them.
Work through an instructor-led bugle exercise focused on accurate notes and timing.
Demonstrate instrument care and rehearse calls for a supervised band performance.

name: Drummers
summary: Build percussion skills through rhythm exercises, music theory, instrument care, and practical band performance.
learn: Accurate percussion playing at different beats and tempos
Music theory, sight-reading, and instrument maintenance
Experience on additional percussion instruments at Advanced level
classActivities: Practise a percussion exercise at different tempos while keeping a steady beat.
Read a simple rhythm with the instructor and play it with a small ensemble.
Explore an additional percussion instrument and demonstrate its correct care.

name: Pipers
summary: Develop bagpipe musicianship through prescribed movements, theory, instrument care, and active band participation.
learn: Bagpipe doublings and grace notes across the prescribed range
Music theory, sight-reading, and instrument care
More advanced bagpipe movements and confident band performance
classActivities: Practise instructor-selected doublings and grace-note exercises.
Read and rehearse a simple passage while working on steady timing.
Demonstrate instrument care and rehearse contrasting pieces with the band.

name: Camping
summary: Develop confident outdoor living through tent work, campsite planning, hygiene, cooking, knots, and equipment care.
learn: Choosing a campsite and pitching, striking, and caring for tents
Camp hygiene, sanitation, food preparation, and equipment storage
Knots, lashings, and useful camp gadgets
classActivities: Practise pitching, striking, and packing a tent as an instructor-supervised team.
Draw a campsite layout that considers cooking, washing, water, waste, and safety.
Practise prescribed knots and lashings, then build a simple camp gadget with guidance.

name: Citizenship
summary: Explore responsible citizenship by studying government, the justice system, or public issues and the agencies addressing them.
learn: An approved topic in government, justice, drug-abuse prevention, or crime prevention
The roles of relevant government agencies and supporting organisations
Ways citizens can contribute to public efforts and community responsibility
classActivities: Choose one handbook topic and prepare an introductory classroom presentation.
Map the relevant agencies and NGOs, identifying their roles and contact points.
Plan a supervised agency visit and discuss practical ways to support its work.

name: Communication
summary: Develop clear personal and public communication through interviews, presentations, discussions and other practical formats.
learn: Build listening, conversation and public-speaking skills.
Explore communication history and formats such as storytelling, media and visual presentations.
Apply communication skills in interviews and an approved public-communication activity.
classActivities: Practise asking open questions in pairs, then prepare an interview outline for an approved adult.
Create a short presentation with visual aids and give it to a squad for feedback.
Take turns moderating a group discussion while classmates practise listening and responding clearly.

name: Community Service
summary: Understand local service organisations and take an active, reflective role in meeting community needs.
learn: Understand the work of community organisations and the people they support.
Plan and carry out practical volunteering or a service project.
Evaluate a project's effects on its recipients and reflect on personal learning.
classActivities: Research a local service organisation and present who it helps and how volunteers contribute.
Plan an officer-approved service project with roles, resources and a record of service hours.
Prepare a report or visual presentation evaluating the project and what members learned.

name: Computer Knowledge
summary: Explore personal and cloud computing and use digital tools to produce a useful, officer-approved project.
learn: Explain personal-computing hardware, software and current developments.
Combine tools such as documents, spreadsheets, presentation software or digital design in a project.
Explore cloud computing and advanced digital projects that benefit the Company.
classActivities: Compare the roles of hardware and software, then present a selected personal-computing topic.
Create an approved project using two software categories, such as a spreadsheet budget and presentation.
Prototype a Company resource using an approved tool such as video editing, web development or an Internet-of-Things device.

name: Environmental Conservation
summary: Learn how daily choices, recycling and practical conservation work can help protect the environment.
learn: Apply the minimum-impact code and identify opportunities to reuse and recycle materials.
Explain how rubbish can harm wildlife and how energy use affects conservation.
Investigate conservation issues and contribute to a local environmental project.
classActivities: Research local recycling options and design a reuse idea for an everyday household item.
Build a conservation scrapbook with thoughtful comments on selected articles.
Interview a conservation group and help plan a supervised cleanup, planting or habitat-improvement activity.

name: Expedition
summary: Build outdoor self-sufficiency through route planning, navigation, lightweight camping and supervised expeditions.
learn: Pack suitable equipment and plan a route using a map and compass.
Practise campcraft, outdoor cooking and responsible care for the countryside.
Develop expedition safety, accident procedures and basic survival skills; First Aid is a prerequisite.
classActivities: Work in teams to plan a route and prepare a rucksack checklist for officer review.
Pitch and strike a tent, then practise planning and preparing a simple camp meal.
Practise map-and-compass navigation on a supervised route and keep a journey log.

name: Financial Stewardship
summary: Connect biblical stewardship with personal budgeting, responsible financial decisions and accountable project finance.
learn: Explore biblical principles of ownership, saving, purposeful spending, giving and tithing.
Prepare personal budgets, track expenses and reflect on financial habits.
Consider debt, investment risk and the integrity needed to manage project finances.
classActivities: Use a sample allowance to prepare a budget for spending, saving and giving.
Practise expense tracking and prepare to maintain the required three-month personal budget and reflection record.
Compare debt and investment scenarios, then build a sample event budget with an officer.

name: Fire and Rescue
summary: Understand fire prevention, emergency escape and rescue equipment through appropriate professional instruction.
learn: Recognise common fire causes, fire classifications and methods of extinguishing fires.
Understand escape from fire and smoke and basic casualty-removal methods.
Explore fire-service organisation, rescue equipment and water supplies.
classActivities: Discuss common fire hazards and practise identifying a safe evacuation route in a classroom scenario.
Arrange a fire-station or Civil Defence visit to learn about equipment and emergency responsibilities.
Practise approved rescue or hose-equipment techniques only with qualified professional supervision.

name: First Aid
summary: Learn to recognise injuries and provide temporary care while awaiting professional treatment under competent first-aid instruction.
learn: Understand a first aider's responsibilities and the basic care of wounds, burns, shock and fractures.
Practise dressings, CPR and other techniques using authorised first-aid teaching materials.
Develop further skills in bandaging, unconscious-casualty care and casualty transport.
classActivities: Practise selecting and applying dressings to simulated injuries with a competent instructor.
Use training equipment to rehearse CPR and unconscious-casualty scenarios under certified supervision.
Discuss injury scenarios and demonstrate appropriate first-aid responses for instructor feedback.

name: Gymnastics
summary: Develop strength, stamina and body control through gymnastics training with a qualified instructor and suitable equipment.
learn: Build controlled movement through selected gymnastics disciplines.
Explore categories such as agility, vaulting, trampoline, bars, strength and stamina.
Progress from two categories at Basic Level to four further categories at Advanced Level.
classActivities: Work with a qualified gymnastics instructor to choose suitable categories and review equipment safety.
Practise instructor-selected agility or apparatus progressions with appropriate supervision and protection.
Keep a training record showing progress in chosen categories and review it with the instructor.

name: International Relations
summary: Discover the worldwide Boys' Brigade family and develop understanding and fellowship across countries and cultures.
learn: Study BB Asia and the Brigade's work in other Asian countries.
Explore the Global Fellowship and BB movements beyond Asia.
Build international understanding through exchanges, correspondence and cultural presentations.
classActivities: Create a country profile with maps, photographs and information about its Boys' Brigade movement.
Prepare a presentation introducing your Company and Malaysian culture for an approved international exchange.
Plan an officer-supervised correspondence project with overseas BB members and share what you learn.

name: Life Saving
summary: Develop water-safety and rescue skills through the Royal Life Saving Society syllabus and supervised practical assessment.
learn: Understand water-safety principles and methods of reaching and throwing rescues.
Develop swimming, rescue, resuscitation and casualty-support skills with qualified instruction.
Progress toward the RLSS Intermediate Certificate and Bronze Medallion standards, with the stated First Aid and Swimming prerequisites.
classActivities: Discuss water-emergency scenarios and select appropriate rescue aids with an instructor.
Practise reaching and throwing rescues in a controlled training setting under qualified supervision.
Complete instructor-led pool sessions to develop the swimming and rescue techniques appropriate to the selected level.

name: Martial Arts
summary: Develop martial-arts skills through regular participation and examinations with an accredited organisation.
learn: Build discipline and technique through consistent, instructor-led practice.
Understand the grading pathway of an accredited martial-arts organisation.
Recognise the handbook's Basic and Advanced belt stages for Judo or Taekwando/Karate.
classActivities: Meet an accredited instructor to discuss the chosen martial art and its grading syllabus.
Practise approved techniques in a properly supervised training session.
Keep an attendance and progress record, then review readiness for an accredited examination with the instructor.

name: Nature Awareness
summary: Explore local habitats and learn to observe, identify and record the plants, animals and natural features found there.
learn: Use maps, a compass and responsible countryside behaviour during nature visits.
Identify flora, fauna and natural specimens using observations and reference books.
Understand how soils, bedrock and environmental conditions shape different habitats.
classActivities: Visit a local habitat with a leader, sketch a map and record the plants and animals observed.
Use field guides to identify photographs or suitable natural specimens and label a nature notebook.
Create a nature scrapbook with sketches, bark rubbings or recorded animal footprints from supervised visits.

name: Physical Training
summary: Build physical fitness and confidence through properly guided training, personal improvement and opportunities to lead others.
learn: Understand training principles and the purpose of warming up and warming down.
Explore how the body responds to aerobic and anaerobic training.
Track age-appropriate personal progress and develop the ability to lead a training session.
classActivities: Join an instructor-led session that demonstrates warm-up, training and warm-down phases.
Keep a progress log during supervised circuit or movement-training sessions.
Prepare an instructor-approved training plan and practise leading suitable activities with the group.

name: Safety
summary: Learn to recognise everyday hazards, promote accident prevention and make responsible choices in physical and digital spaces.
learn: Recognise hazards at home, school, on roads, around water and during sport.
Assess risks and communicate practical accident-prevention messages.
Explore digital citizenship, privacy, cybersecurity, cyberbullying and identity theft.
classActivities: Discuss illustrated everyday scenarios and identify hazards and prevention measures.
Carry out an officer-guided risk assessment of the Company parade meeting place.
Prepare a school or church safety campaign, or present a researched cyber-safety topic to the group.

name: Sustainability
summary: Connect the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals with practical projects that benefit the local community.
learn: Relate local community needs to the Sustainable Development Goals.
Plan and carry out a community project with a positive, observable impact.
Document project work and collaborate more widely at the Advanced stage.
classActivities: Choose a local need, match it to an SDG and prepare a project plan with assigned roles.
Take part in an officer-guided community project and record sessions, contributions and outcomes.
Present the project's impact and reflections through a written report, slides or a video presentation.

name: Social Entrepreneurship
summary: Explore how an enterprise can address community needs, then study or develop a venture with a positive social impact.
learn: Connect a community problem with a practical enterprise-based solution.
Consider goals, stakeholders, finances and effects on the local community.
Evaluate outcomes and reflect on learning from a social-enterprise project.
classActivities: Research an existing social enterprise and present its goals, approach, finances and community impact.
Develop a proposed community enterprise and seek the Company Officer's approval before carrying it out.
Prepare a project presentation explaining the problem, solution, stakeholders, results and lessons learned.

name: Sports
summary: Develop sporting ability through sustained training, participation in recognised competitions and evidence of personal progress.
learn: Understand the history, rules and wider context of a chosen sport.
Improve performance through regular training and active competition.
Progress to stronger competition or develop another eligible sport at the Advanced stage.
classActivities: Join a coached practice session for a chosen sport other than swimming or athletics and record personal progress.
Prepare a short explanation of the sport's history, rules and competition structure.
Take part in an appropriate Company or school competition and discuss performance with the coach or officer.

name: Swimming
summary: Develop swimming technique and work towards the handbook's Basic and Advanced performance standards under qualified supervision.
learn: Improve freestyle, breaststroke, backstroke or butterfly technique.
Understand the swimming events and performance standards used for assessment.
Build water confidence through properly supervised instruction and progression.
classActivities: Attend a qualified-instructor-led stroke session in a supervised swimming pool.
Record progress in instructor-approved timed and distance swimming practice.
Review the relevant Basic or Advanced assessment areas and individual readiness with the swimming instructor.

name: Water Adventure
summary: Build skills and safety awareness in a chosen water activity, using canoeing as the handbook's example syllabus.
learn: Understand the Swimming Award prerequisite and the emphasis on skill and water safety.
Explore canoe types, maintenance, storage and supervised craft-handling skills.
Learn about canoe camping, local access rules and progression to more advanced paddling.
classActivities: Identify different canoe types and discuss their history, safe storage and maintenance with an instructor.
Join a qualified-instructor-led session to practise approved canoe handling and paddling skills.
Plan a canoe-camping scenario and discuss safety, local rules, access and equipment care with the instructor.
